screen_plans.name: Reporting Setup Page
screen_plans.purpose: The module's entry point. A person picks one of three report types, finds a report in that type's list, and switches reports on or off.
user_flows: Open Reporting Setup Page -> pick a report type tab -> see that tab's list with its count badge -> filter, search or page the list -> open a report
Open Reporting Setup Page -> find the report -> switch active off -> delivery stops, and switching on later does not backfill
screen_plans.notes: Application-resident in the Sand Generation shell, not platform-level. The tab bar stays mounted and usable in the loading, empty and error states; only the list body substitutes.

screen_plans.name: Report Editor
screen_plans.purpose: Define one report: its source dashboard, what it covers, the period, the output format, the schedule and the recipients. The source picker comes first because every other field depends on it.
user_flows: Open Report Editor -> choose one saved dashboard as source -> source name shows on screen -> coverage options resolve as visibly pending -> choose coverage kind -> choose covered scopes
In Report Editor -> choose PDF or Excel -> if PDF, choose diagrams and tables, diagrams only, or tables only -> set the period
In Report Editor -> choose repeating or one-time -> set start date -> set time of day -> read the declared time zone -> choose repeat interval
In Report Editor -> add a recipient address -> address shows as inside or outside the organization -> repeat per address -> switch active on
Open a report -> request generate once -> one file produced -> one delivery sent -> one run recorded
screen_plans.notes: Ordered by dependency. Coverage cannot resolve until a source is chosen, so progressive disclosure is required rather than stylistic. OPEN DECISION 1 may move the schedule fields to a separate step, and OPEN DECISION 6 decides the recipient list's form.

screen_plans.name: Run History
screen_plans.purpose: Show when a report ran, what it covered, which file it produced, who received it, and whether it worked — so somebody can find out that last night's report did not send, and why.
user_flows: Open a report -> open Run History -> runs listed newest first -> read outcome, recipients as sent, and file reference
screen_plans.notes: OPEN DECISION 4 decides whether this sits per report or centrally. Empty and error substitute into the table body without unmounting the surrounding report.

screen_plans.name: Make a Report from This Dashboard
screen_plans.purpose: Start a report already bound to the dashboard the person is looking at, without leaving it.
user_flows: Open a dashboard -> choose Make a Report from This -> form opens with the source pre-chosen -> complete the minimum -> save
screen_plans.notes: No empty or partial-data state — it is always reached from a dashboard that exists. OPEN DECISION 5 decides whether this is a short form or a navigation to the full Report Editor; either way the error path lands on the setup page with the source pre-chosen, so both surfaces exist.

screen_plans.name: Dashboard Deletion Impact Dialog
screen_plans.purpose: Before a dashboard is deleted, name every scheduled report that depends on it and how many, and require a second deliberate action to proceed.
user_flows: Delete a source dashboard -> Dashboard Deletion Impact Dialog names every dependent report and how many -> confirm as a second deliberate action -> those reports go inactive with the reason recorded
screen_plans.notes: Sits inside a deletion flow owned by the dashboard builders — OPEN DECISION 9. The PRD's own screen inventory omits this surface entirely, though Requirements 21 and 43-45 require it.

screen_plans.name: Report PDF Output
screen_plans.purpose: The produced PDF, in each of its three content variants. A design surface nobody clicks, which still has to say whose view of the portfolio it holds.
user_flows: A recipient opens the attachment and can tell which dashboard and whose authority it came from
screen_plans.notes: Three variants: diagrams and tables, diagrams only, tables only. No loading or forbidden state — it is a file, not a screen.

screen_plans.name: Report Excel Workbook Output

screen_plans.name: Report Delivery Email
screen_plans.purpose: The message the report arrives in. The PRD names it a fifth design surface requiring a design rather than a default.
user_flows: Schedule fires -> authority resolved at the run -> file rendered -> delivery recorded -> Report Delivery Email sent with attachment
screen_plans.notes: Nothing partial ever sends. No empty, loading, forbidden or partial-data state.

primary_flows: Find a report: Reporting Setup Page -> type tab -> list -> open a report
Define a report: Report Editor -> source -> coverage -> period -> format -> schedule -> recipients -> switch on
Report from a dashboard: dashboard -> Make a Report from This -> source pre-chosen -> save
Run once now: open a report -> generate once -> one file, one delivery, one run recorded
Scheduled delivery: schedule fires -> authority resolved -> file rendered -> delivery recorded -> email sent
Diagnose a failure: open a report -> Run History -> outcome, recipients as sent, reason
Stop a report: Reporting Setup Page -> active switch off -> no backfill on resume
Delete a source: dashboard deletion -> Dashboard Deletion Impact Dialog -> second confirmation -> dependents go inactive
critical_paths: Source dashboard -> coverage constrained by that source -> format -> schedule in a declared time zone -> at least one recipient -> active on
Schedule fires -> authority resolved at the run -> delivery recorded BEFORE sending -> email sent -> run outcome readable in Run History
Authority loses access to a covered site -> next run does not send -> report goes inactive with the reason recorded
Source dashboard deleted -> dependents named and counted -> second confirmation -> dependents inactive, no file sent
information_architecture.notes: Eight surfaces, of which three (Report PDF Output, Report Excel Workbook Output, Report Delivery Email) are produced artefacts rather than screens and therefore carry no loading or forbidden state. The Dashboard Deletion Impact Dialog is required by REQ-43 to REQ-45 but is absent from the PRD's own screen inventory. Thirteen requirements are deliberately not mapped to any element because they are backend or cross-cutting rules with no interface manifestation: REQ-9, REQ-11, REQ-16, REQ-18, REQ-29, REQ-30, REQ-46, REQ-48, REQ-59, REQ-77, REQ-104, REQ-106, REQ-108.
